transfer_provisions.quote: Enlisted members who are being subsisted in kind in a mess and whose duties require them to be absent from their station during one or more meals shall be entitled for each such meal to a pro-rated share of the daily basic allowance for subsistence
transfer_provisions.note: Sec. 301 repeats sec. 1 of EO 10119 as amended by EO 10605; secs. 302-303 repeat secs. 2-3 (supplemental regulations; definitions) with the citation moved to 37 U.S.C. 402. This is a successor re-prescription of the revoked regulations, not a savings clause.

effective_date_reading: Sec. 502 says 'The following Executive orders are revoked' and no effective-date wording appears anywhere in the order (Parts I-V read in full). The revocations took effect on signing, June 22, 1964 (printed 29 FR 7973-7980, June 24, 1964).

targets_in_batch_03.EO:10119: sec. 502(a) ('Executive Order No. 10119 of March 27, 1950'); sec. 502(e) revokes EO 10605, the amendment of EO 10119

conclusion: EO 11157 (signed 1964-06-22, 29 FR 7973-7980, PDF pages 7-14, read once in full) prescribes regulations for incentive pay for hazardous duty (Part I), sea-duty and certain-places pay (Part II), basic allowances for subsistence (Part III) and for quarters (Part IV), with general provisions (Part V). Sec. 502 revokes thirteen Executive orders by number, including EO 10119 (a) and its amendment EO 10605 (e). It has no savings, continuation, pending-matter or exception clause and no effective-date wording. Part III (secs. 301-303) re-prescribes the subsistence-allowance rules of EO 10119 as amended, so the revoked order's content is carried into the successor order. Secs. 113, 208, 302 and 407 authorise the Secretaries to issue supplementary regulations; they are new grants, not savings.

batch_05_reread.whole_not_partial: Sec. 502 lists thirteen Executive orders by number and date with no section limit, no 'except' wording and no 'as amended' limit, so each of 10204, 10618 and 10821 is revoked whole. The machine ACT records mark these 'partial' only because their quoted span runs through Parts III-V up to sec. 502(d) and the dossier labels it 'Sec. 302'.
batch_05_reread.successor_parts: The sections of EO 11157 that re-prescribe the revoked orders' content: Part I (secs. 101 ff., hazardous-duty incentive pay) carries the definitions that EO 10152 sec. 9 had as amended by EO 10618, EO 10739 and EO 11120 (sec. 109(b) repeats the 10618 text of sec. 9(b); 109(c)-(e) the later (e), (f) and (h)); Part II (secs. 201 ff., sea-duty and certain-places pay) repeats the sea-duty definitions of EO 10168 as amended by EO 10821, EO 10989 and EO 11120 (sec. 202(a)-(b) and 203 repeat the 10821 wording of secs. 2 and 3, with the 10989 clauses (5)-(6) added); Part IV (secs. 401-408) repeats the quarters regulations of EO 10204 as amended by EO 11120 and EO 11146. Each is a successor re-prescription under title 37 U.S.C., not a savings clause.
batch_05_reread.no_effective_wording: Parts I-V were read again for effective-date, savings and continuation wording (batch 05): none appears, so the secs. 502(d), (f), (i) revocations took effect on signing, June 22, 1964 (printed 29 FR 7973-7980, June 24, 1964).
batch_05_reread.supplementary_regulations: Secs. 113, 208, 302 and 407 authorise the Secretaries to issue supplementary regulations 'not inconsistent herewith'. Supplementary regulations issued under the revoked orders are not revoked by sec. 502 in terms.
